label: copy phase, from the 3rd output onward
explanation: Positional copy-phase feature. Fires almost only during the copy phase (100% of mass; essentially never on original tokens or the <DEL> step), turning on from recall_idx 2 (rate 0.78) and rising to ~0.97 by recall_idx 8. At recall_idx 1 it is weak (rate 0.16, 1.6% of mass). Activation grows as the copy continues: in top examples it ramps across the copy phase, and longer sequences and later recall positions carry more mass. Copy-phase input token 1 has the largest mass share (0.099 against ~0.03-0.05 for other tokens), and the top examples peak on a fed-back 1. Apart from that it does not depend much on token identity (in_tok, out_tok, first_tok lift are all flat). False positives are mostly at early copy steps (recall_idx 2-3) in short sequences.

issues: Core claims check out. Activation mass by phase: original 0.000, delimiter 0.000, copy 1.000. Firing rate by recall_idx: 0.16 at 1, 0.775 at 2, 0.82 at 3, 0.90 at 4, rising to 0.976 at 8. Test score: P 0.875, R 0.960, F1 0.916, mass recall 0.984, which matches the report.

The explanation's claim that 'false positives are mostly early copy steps in short sequences' is wrong about length. At recall_idx 2, precision is 0.84 for L<=4 and 0.77 for L>=7, so short sequences are not where the problem lies. The false positives sit at early recall_idx (2-3) and late in the sequence (to_go>=5 precision 0.80, to_go<=2 precision 0.90) at every length.

'Token identity matters little' overstates it. A fed-back 'g' suppresses the feature: precision is 0.50 for (phase==2)&(recall_idx>=2)&(in_tok==g), against 0.87 overall, and 0.36 at recall_idx 2-3. Fed-back b, e, w, x and q at recall_idx 2 also give precision of about 0.60-0.65. In the other direction, prev_tok==1 at recall_idx 2 gives 0.97. These steps are a small fraction of the copy phase, though. Excluding g at recall_idx<=3 moves dev F1 only from 0.915 to 0.917, so this is token modulation, not a counterexample class.

The 'ramps up' claim holds only loosely. Activation is not monotonic within a sequence: test examples show dips and dropouts in the middle of the copy, e.g. 'h e n n 0 r g i h' goes silent at several steps. The misses (1.6% of mass) are scattered weak activations at recall_idx 1 with no clear pattern.
